subject: Performance SLO / Private VPC follow-up — network & streaming requirements
messages:
From: Tom Richards <tom.richards@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo follow-up — performance SLOs / private VPC

Thanks for the demo today — that was really helpful. A few follow-ups from our infra and product teams so we can validate feasibility on our side before the technical deep-dive: 

- Latency: We want to confirm whether Redwood can meet a 95th percentile end-to-end latency <= 350ms for single-response generation up to ~512 tokens (first-byte and tail). Is that realistic on a private VPC deployment or would we need dedicated capacity?
- Concurrency & throughput: Our initial traffic estimate is ~100 concurrent active sessions with bursts to ~300 for short periods. What's the expected throughput and any guidance on autoscaling behavior for private deployments?
- Streaming: We need first-byte streaming within 200ms for chat UX. Does Redwood support chunked streaming over HTTP/2 or TCP with minimal buffering?
- Network path: We're planning an AWS Direct Connect/Transit/On-prem setup — we'll likely peer with Redwood or establish VPN tunnels. Key asks: what egress IP ranges do you need open, MTU considerations (we saw issues in the past), and are there any requirements for mutual TLS?

I've attached our current network diagram for context (acme-network-diagram.pdf). Happy to schedule an infra call — Jordan suggested a technical handshake next week.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Richards
SRE Lead, Acme Corporation

--
Attachment: acme-network-diagram.pdf (application/pdf, 310KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Richards <tom.richards@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Post-demo follow-up — performance SLOs / private VPC

Thanks Tom — great questions and appreciated the network diagram. Quick recap + proposed next steps so everyone's aligned: 

Recap of our guidance (initial, to be validated in tech deep-dive):
- Latency SLOs: For Private/VPC deployments we can target p95 <= 350ms for typical single-response requests up to 512 tokens when colocated with a Dedicated pool. For hosted small instances, p95 may be higher depending on contention. We will validate with a perf run on your topology.
- First-byte streaming: We support chunked streaming (server-sent chunks over HTTPS) with sub-200ms first-byte in normal network conditions — we'll include a small experiment during the perf window to measure TTFB.
- Concurrency & throughput: Given your burst profile, plan for steady-state 100 concurrent, burst to 300. For private deployments we recommend reserving a Dedicated pool sized for burst headroom (we'll include numbers in the proposal).
- Network requirements (initial): 
  - Ports: 443 outbound (TLS) to Redwood peering endpoints; spurious control ports may use 5222 for internal control plane if needed (we'll confirm).
  - Egress IPs: We'll provide a list of ASN / IP ranges you'll need to allow for peering/VPN.
  - MTU: Keep default 1500; if you're using IPSEC tunnels check for PMTUD issues — we'll include an iperf/MTU check in tests.
  - Latency budget internal to your app: to meet p95 <= 350ms we generally see network hop budget <= 20ms round-trip between your app and the Redwood VPC endpoint (application-level processing excluded).

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical deep-dive with Jordan (network/infra) + our infra eng (Aditya) — propose Tue Dec 7, 10:00 AM PT (we can adjust).
2) Exchange egress IP ranges + temporary ACLs so we can run an iperf + HTTP streaming test during a 2-hour perf window.
3) I'll attach an initial SLO/size proposal (redwood-slo-proposal-v1.pdf) for your review; we'll iterate after the perf run.

Attached: redwood-slo-proposal-v1.pdf (draft).

If that timeline works, Jordan/Aditya and I will set up invites and a perf checklist.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redwood-slo-proposal-v1.pdf (application/pdf, 120KB)

From: Tom Richards <tom.richards@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T10:42:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Post-demo follow-up — performance SLOs / private VPC

Thanks Marissa — that plan sounds good. A few answers from our side to help Jordan/Aditya prep: 

- Concurrency: Our current telemetry (canary) shows ~85 steady concurrent websocket sessions and we can tolerate ~250 concurrent for short bursts. If you size for 300 burst, that would cover our expected peak.
- Internal latency: Most app servers in our primary region (us-west-2) have 2–5ms RTT to the edge load balancer; cross-AZ adds ~3–4ms. Between our edge and your proposed peering location we're seeing ~8–12ms RTT in recent traces.
- VPN/Peering: We prefer to establish a private peering link (Transit Gateway / Direct Connect) to avoid NAT egress churn. We can also support IPSEC tunnel if that's simpler initially.
- Mutual TLS: We can support mTLS; would Redwood require client certs for the data plane or only for control-plane authentication?

I've attached a short traceroute/packet-capture around our peering point (network-trace-tunnel.png). Let us know if you need more details on BGP or ASN.

Tom

--
Attachment: network-trace-tunnel.png (image/png, 85KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T16:10:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Prep checklist for ACME perf run

Internal checklist for the infra call / perf window (Jordan -> Marissa/Aditya):

- Provide Acme the temporary egress IP ranges (we'll use these for iptables/ACLs).
- Confirm whether Acme will do Direct Connect/Transit peering or IPSEC tunnel; plan both test flows.
- Perf tests to run: iperf3 (TCP + UDP), HTTP streaming TTFB tests (simulated chat), 512-token generation wall-clock time, tail-latency percentile snapshots (p50/p95/p99).
- Logging & tracing: ensure we enable header-level tracing so we can tie request IDs across their app and our runtime.
- MTU check & PMTUD: set up small MTU sweep if they are using tunnels.
- Ports: 443 outbound; ensure no deep packet inspection proxys that might buffer streaming chunks (ask Acme SRE).
- Data plane auth: prefer mTLS for control plane; for data plane we can accept TLS with client certs if they require mutual auth — Aditya to confirm timeframe for cert exchange.

I'll draft the perf run script and share it with Marissa to send to Tom. Also will propose Tue Dec 7 10:00 AM PT for the deep-dive (fits our eng availability).

- Jordan

(Internal note: keep Acme engagement owner on Marissa -> follow through with HubSpot record & send calendar invite once Tom confirms.)
